### 2026-10-29: # Research

**3.75h**

# Research
## The Powerhouse
I started off looking at esp32 because I am more familiar with them, because I want to use a 7 inch IPS display, I thought using the p4 or p4x would be a smart move, because p4 have lots of flash and psram, and are powerful. However they seem expensive and not readily available unfortunately.

![1000009102](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/91HF73JHUwEio9xtrq7tRJvOd8KiT0lT/9861753ab12c96cdd695d51ae0f80cb66571478ebbf503e0988d7d6dda84f6c1.jpg)

Then I look towards SBC, single board computer, which would give me much more computer power, if I got a SBC, I would have to pair it with a esp32 C6 or something small to allow it to communicate to the controllers more easily, via esp-now or Bluetooth. But since I wanted to make a game console with satellite controllers, I figured that the SBC with extra board cost too much. I did look at the Raspberry pi 3 model b for a while but it cost more than $20 alone without having the power supply, etc.. I would have liked to use a SBC but it probably would have created unnecessary hassle. It is a drawback I am fine making for this project.

![1000009064](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/91HF73JHUwEio9xtrq7tRJvOd8KiT0lT/797877c6a675fcb1b19df5a5fc4948176e2e7b6d37f0352f0da13a48cb6d76aa.jpg)

## Decision
In the end, I think a esp32 S3 LCD driver and a screen will be my best bet. It is a good price and is still powerful enough to run a LCD touchscreen. I also looked a a few bundle but am still undecided whether to buy sperately or together, and with a IPS or TN screen. I want to go with the largest screen I can. Esp32 S3 have also been around for a while and are quite supported by the espresiff community. I may use one like in the picture below.

![1000009085](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/91HF73JHUwEio9xtrq7tRJvOd8KiT0lT/6d68a03f64de0800137769ae0553be80322c1a6c2d4a56f9784ae0ccf03ccef9.jpg)

## Batteries
I also looked at batteries, I decided to go for 18650s because they are good, durable, batteries with metal shielding and have good capacity. I looked at high amp, low capacity ones like 30A, 2500mah ones, and low amp high capacity ones like 10A 3500mah. I decided for my controller I will only use 1, to create a good balance of weight and battery life time. For the screen I will probably do a 2p setup to maximise capacity. For both I will use a boost converter to step it up to a clean 5v for the esp to function. I will probably use 10A 3500mah ones if I can.

![1000009214](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/91HF73JHUwEio9xtrq7tRJvOd8KiT0lT/a93c7f688a8169e111d3a500d903f53fa0dd2ccebd4ec556f4527792f55ed8c1.jpg)

### 2026-10-30: ## PCB layout

**6h**

## PCB layout
I had a struggle figuring out a good layout, the pieces started in a jumbled mess but after 3 iterations and a hand drawn sketch, I figured out a rough layout and then translated it onto my computer. I tried my best to keep everything symmetrical and neat. I wired the GND through a copper pour, and I did the copper pour in the top and bottom layer to reduce electrical interference.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/91HF73JHUwEio9xtrq7tRJvOd8KiT0lT/59f3ca1de7fb952d837fe1cd81a2139bfbdaf6207fee9d460ab8993a1e16b17e.png)
